Action Plan:
1. Book an in-person appointment with the support team for a full neurological examination, including fundoscopy and blood pressure measurement; cancel appointment if symptoms settle before scheduled date.
2. Prescribe a stronger analgesic than ibuprofen (medication name not documented — dose/route/frequency not documented) and advise concurrent paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); instruct patient to take medication(s) with food.
3. Check blood pressure at the in-person appointment to assess continued suitability of the oral contraceptive pill; continue current pill for now unless migraine with aura is confirmed, in which case change of contraception may be required.
4. Advise patient to attend Emergency Department (A&E) immediately if headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes in character; patient may call the clinic for further advice beforehand.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for 3 days, woke with headache 3 days ago; persistent and interfering with work.
- Headache characteristics:
  - Onset: sudden.
  - Duration: continuous over past 3 days.
  - Location: diffuse, stronger over the right eye.
  - Severity: reported as 8/10 at worst, decreases to ~5/10 at times.
  - Pattern: present most of the time; partially relieved but not resolved by ibuprofen.
  - Aggravating factors: bright lights (photophobia), standing up quickly causing brief stabbing pain, head movement sensations.
  - Associated symptoms: photophobia, transient visual phenomena described as “shooting light”; feeling slightly sick but no vomiting; sleep not disturbed by headache.
- Past headache history: occasional short headaches in past (one lasted two days responsive to ibuprofen); no prior episodes of this severity.
- Past medical history: none significant reported; childhood pain episode with no cause found.
- Medications: oral contraceptive pill (specific pill not documented); ibuprofen taken intermittently for headache; paracetamol mentioned for concurrent use (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social history: lives alone; works from home (missed some work due to headache); does not smoke; drinks alcohol about once per week (patient estimated “probably like three [drinks] once a week”).
- Family history: mother has migraines with vomiting.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during this consultation.
- No vital signs recorded.
- No investigations performed during this consultation.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis:
     - Migraine-type headache.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Migraine with aura (considered because of visual phenomena).
     - Other primary headache disorders; secondary causes to be excluded on examination.
   - Investigations planned:
     - In-person neurological examination.
     - Fundoscopic (back of eye) examination.
     - Blood pressure measurement.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Prescription of a stronger analgesic than ibuprofen (medication name not documented — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Paracetamol concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Take medications with food.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Appointment to be booked with support team for above assessment.
     - Possible specialist referral (e.g., neurology) to be considered after examination if indicated.

2. Oral contraceptive pill suitability
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis:
     - Current pill continued; suitability to be reassessed if migraine with aura is confirmed.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Not applicable beyond need to assess presence/absence of migraine aura.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Blood pressure check at the in-person appointment.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue current oral contraceptive pill for now.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - None arranged at this time; change of contraception may be arranged if migraine with aura is diagnosed.

  - No vital signs (blood pressure, temperature, pulse) recorded.

  - Precise alcohol intake quantity unclear.
